days.label: Analects 1.1 to 1.16
days.key: The Master said, ‘Is it not pleasant to learn with a constant perseverance and application?
days.s: The book opens with the Master’s three questions, on learning, distant friends and calm when unknown; Zhu Xi, on 1.1, reads learning as imitating those who awoke first, to understand the good and recover an original goodness, and the application as a bird’s repeated flights.
days.src: Zhu Xi, Lunyu jizhu, on 1.1, zh.wikisource (Sishu zhangju jizhu, Lunyu jizhu juan 1), revision 2598582 (2025)

days.label: Analects 2.1 to 2.24
days.key: The Master said, ‘Learning without thought is labour lost; thought without learning is perilous.’
days.s: Among sayings on learning and knowing, just before a warning against strange doctrines, the Master pairs study with reflection; He Yan, on 2.15, takes the peril of thinking without study as weariness, for such thought gets nothing in the end and wears out the spirit.
days.src: He Yan, Lunyu jijie, on 2.15, zh.wikisource (Lunyu jijie/01, proofread), revision 2270598 (2023)

days.label: Analects 3.1 to 3.26
days.key: The Master said, ‘Not so. He who offends against Heaven has none to whom he can pray.’
days.s: Asked by Wang-sun Chia about a proverb preferring the furnace to the south-west corner, the Master rejects it; Zhu Xi, on 3.13, reads Heaven as principle: no prayer to corner or furnace clears one who defies it, so one should follow principle and court neither.
days.src: Zhu Xi, Lunyu jizhu, on 3.13, zh.wikisource (Sishu zhangju jizhu, Lunyu jizhu juan 2), revision 2063643 (2021)

days.label: Analects 4.1 to 4.26
days.key: The Master said, ‘The faults of men are characteristic of the class to which they belong. By observing a man’s faults, it may be known that he is virtuous.’
days.s: After lamenting that no lover of virtue is seen, the Master turns to failings; He Yan’s collection, on 4.7, gives Kong Anguo’s reading, which takes the small man’s falling short of the gentleman as no fault, and fitting each to his place as virtue.
days.src: He Yan, Lunyu jijie (Kong Anguo’s gloss), on 4.7, zh.wikisource (Lunyu jijie/02, proofread), revision 2270600 (2023)

days.label: Analects 5.1 to 5.27
days.key: The Master said, ‘In a hamlet of ten families, there may be found one honourable and sincere as I am, but not so fond of learning.’
days.s: Ending a book that weighs disciples and officers, the Master speaks of himself; Zhu Xi, on 5.27, reads it as a spur to others: fine endowments are easily found, the highest Way hard to hear, and learning carried through can make a sage.
days.src: Zhu Xi, Lunyu jizhu, on 5.27, zh.wikisource (Sishu zhangju jizhu, Lunyu jizhu juan 3), revision 2281474 (2023)

days.label: Analects 6.1 to 6.28
days.key: He did not transfer his anger; he did not repeat a fault.
days.s: Asked by the Duke Ai which disciple loved learning, Confucius names Yen Hui; He Yan, on 6.2, reads him as led by the Way where ordinary men follow feeling, his anger kept to its due and never shifted, and no wrong ever done twice.
days.src: He Yan, Lunyu jijie, on 6.2, zh.wikisource (Lunyu jijie/03, proofread), revision 2270601 (2023)

days.label: Analects 7.1 to 7.37
days.key: The Master said, ‘My praying has been for a long time.’
days.s: Gravely ill, asked by Tsze-lu for leave to pray, the Master replies; Zhu Xi, on 7.34, reads it as an indirect refusal: prayer is repentance and amendment to seek the spirits’ help, and a sage whose conduct accorded with them had nothing to repent.
days.src: Zhu Xi, Lunyu jizhu, on 7.34, zh.wikisource (Sishu zhangju jizhu, juan 4), revision 2285801 (2023)

days.label: Analects 8.1 to 8.21
days.key: The Master said, ‘Learn as if you could not reach your object, and were always fearing also lest you should lose it.’
days.s: Between a saying on the ardent who are not upright and praise of Shun and Yu, the Master gives a charge on study; He Yan, on 8.17, explains that learning enters from outside and lasts only when thoroughly ripened, hence the fear of losing it.
days.src: He Yan, Lunyu jijie, on 8.17, zh.wikisource (the Jijie notes in Lunyu zhushu, juan 8), revision 7904524 (2026)

days.label: Analects 9.1 to 9.30
days.key: The Master said, ‘When the year becomes cold, then we know how the pine and the cypress are the last to lose their leaves.’
days.s: After praising Tsze-lu’s unashamed poverty, the Master turns to trees in the cold; He Yan, on 9.27, reads it as a figure: in settled times common men also order themselves, and only a muddied age makes the gentleman’s uprightness known.
days.src: He Yan, Lunyu jijie, on 9.27, zh.wikisource (the Jijie notes in Lunyu zhushu, juan 9), revision 2030329 (2021)

days.label: Analects 10.1 to 10.18
days.key: The stable being burned down, when he was at court, on his return he said, ‘Has any man been hurt?’ He did not ask about the horses.
days.s: In a book of his ways at court, at table and at home, a stable burns; Zhu Xi, on 10.12, reads the silence about horses not as indifference but as fear for people leaving no leisure to ask, since principle values people above beasts.
days.src: Zhu Xi, Lunyu jizhu, on 10.12, zh.wikisource (Sishu zhangju jizhu, juan 5), revision 2018280 (2021)

days.label: Analects 11.1 to 11.25
days.key: The Master said, ‘While you are not able to serve men, how can you serve their spirits?’ Chi Lu added, ‘I venture to ask about death?’ He was answered, ‘While you do not know life, how can you know about death?’
days.s: Chi Lu asks how to serve the spirits of the dead, then about death; He Yan’s collection, on 11.11, gives Chen Qun, who takes both replies as declining to answer, since spirits and death are hard to make clear and talk of them profits nothing.
days.src: He Yan, Lunyu jijie, Chen Qun’s gloss on 11.11, zh.wikisource (the Jijie notes in Lunyu zhushu, juan 11), revision 1375235 (2018)

days.label: Analects 12.1 to 12.24
days.key: The Master said, ‘To subdue one’s self and return to propriety, is perfect virtue.
days.s: Yen Yuan asks about perfect virtue, and the Master answers, then lists four prohibitions; Zhu Xi, on 12.1, reads the self as the body’s selfish desires and propriety as the ordered pattern of heavenly principle, whose recovery makes the heart’s virtue whole again.
days.src: Zhu Xi, Lunyu jizhu, on 12.1, zh.wikisource (Sishu zhangju jizhu, juan 6), revision 2358541 (2024)

days.label: Analects 13.1 to 13.30
days.key: The father conceals the misconduct of the son, and the son conceals the misconduct of the father. Uprightness is to be found in this.
days.s: After the Duke of Sheh praises a son who testifies that his father stole a sheep, Confucius answers him; Zhu Xi, on 13.18, reads father and son shielding each other as the utmost of heavenly principle and human feeling, in which uprightness comes unsought.
days.src: Zhu Xi, Lunyu jizhu, on 13.18, zh.wikisource (Sishu zhangju jizhu, Lunyu jizhu juan 7), revision 2412885 (2024)

days.label: Analects 14.1 to 14.21
days.key: The Master said, ‘He who speaks without modesty will find it difficult to make his words good.’
days.s: After judgements on princes and their ministers, the day’s passage closes on a saying about speech; He Yan’s collection, on 14.21, gives Ma Rong, who reads unashamed speech as coming from substance within, and the gathering of that substance as what is hard.
days.src: He Yan, Lunyu jijie, Ma Rong’s gloss on 14.21, zh.wikisource (the jijie notes in Lunyu zhushu, juan 14), revision 2371072 (2024)

days.label: Analects 14.22 to 14.47
days.key: ‘Recompense injury with justice, and recompense kindness with kindness.’
days.s: Asked about repaying injury with kindness, the Master asks what would then repay kindness; Zhu Xi, on 14.36, reads justice here as love and hate, taking and refusing, all ruled by utmost fairness without self-interest, and kindness received as never to be forgotten.
days.src: Zhu Xi, Lunyu jizhu, on 14.36, zh.wikisource (Sishu zhangju jizhu, Lunyu jizhu juan 7), revision 2412885 (2024)

days.label: Analects 15.1 to 15.41
days.key: ‘No,’ was the answer; ‘I seek a unity all-pervading.’
days.s: The Master asks Tsze-kung whether he takes him for a man of wide learning and memory; He Yan, in his own note on 15.2, reads the unity as knowing the origin of every good, so that all are known through one, without much learning.
days.src: He Yan, Lunyu jijie, own note on 15.2, zh.wikisource (the jijie notes in Lunyu zhushu, juan 15), revision 7904695 (2026)

days.label: Analects 16.1 to 16.14
days.key: ‘When right principles prevail in the kingdom, there will be no discussions among the common people.’
days.s: Confucius traces authority slipping from the son of Heaven down to retainers, then turns to the common people; Zhu Xi, on 16.2, reads it as no private criticism below when government above does not fail, not as mouths gagged into silence.
days.src: Zhu Xi, Lunyu jizhu, on 16.2, zh.wikisource (Sishu zhangju jizhu, Lunyu jizhu juan 8), revision 2304542 (2023)

days.label: Analects 17.1 to 17.26
days.key: ‘Am I a bitter gourd! How can I be hung up out of the way of being eaten?’
days.s: Invited by the rebel Pi Hsi, the Master answers Tsze-lu’s protest; He Yan, in his own note on 17.7, reads the gourd as hung in one place because it does not eat, whereas the Master, who eats, must go in every direction.
days.src: He Yan, Lunyu jijie, own note on 17.7, zh.wikisource (the jijie notes in Lunyu zhushu, juan 17), revision 432755 (2015)

days.label: Analects 18.1 to 18.11
days.key: If right principles prevailed through the empire, there would be no use for me to change its state.
days.s: When a recluse urges Tsze-lu to quit a world swept by disorder, the Master sighs that he must keep company with mankind; Zhu Xi, on 18.6, reads him as seeking to change the world by the Way precisely because it lacks the Way.
days.src: Zhu Xi, Lunyu jizhu, on 18.6, zh.wikisource (Sishu zhangju jizhu, juan 9), revision 2560458 (2025)

days.label: Analects 19.1 to 19.25
days.key: When you have found out the truth of any accusation, be grieved for and pity them, and do not feel joy at your own ability.
days.s: Yang Fu, made chief criminal judge, consults the philosopher Tsang, who begins from rulers long failed in their duties; He Yan’s collection, on 19.19, gives Ma Rong, who reads the people’s lawbreaking as the doing of those above, not the people’s own fault.
days.src: He Yan, Lunyu jijie, Ma Rong’s gloss on 19.19, zh.wikisource (Lunyu zhushu, juan 19, the jijie notes), revision 432753 (2015)

days.label: Analects 20.1 to 20.3
days.key: If, in my person, I commit offences, they are not to be attributed to you, the people of the myriad regions. If you in the myriad regions commit offences, these offences must rest on my person.
days.s: Among the words of ancient kings, T’ang, having told God he dare not pardon the sinner, turns to the people; Zhu Xi, on 20.1, reads it as a king who counts their offences truly his own doing, blaming himself heavily and others lightly.
days.src: Zhu Xi, Lunyu jizhu, on 20.1, zh.wikisource (Sishu zhangju jizhu, juan 10), revision 2611553 (2025)
